doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Hard bop and the strength of Benny Golson's compositions
summary: He calls the Jazztet hard bop and praises Golson's writing, such as Stablemates and Whisper Not.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Would that band have gone under the heading of hard bop?

Yeah I would say so because we were playing across things, because you know Benny did a lot of writing of his own. And to this day Benny Golson has never written a weak composition. Every composition that he has written is strong. “Stablemates?” Strong. Challenging. “Along Came Betty?” Strong. “Whisper Not?” Beautiful. “I Remember Clifford?” Beautiful. Most guys don’t play that because a lot of guys don’t know how to play just the melody because they don’t know the difference between the melody in the first thing and secondly I mean it’s very deceptive because Benny Golson is a true genius you know. And when he writes a composition it’s a composition. It’s not a song, it’s a composition that’s been thoroughly worked out and, you know what I mean. And creatively sound.
